{{Quote|Remember what you were saying about 'worse than destroyers?' I think we're looking at them.|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and referring to MagnaGuards|<ref name="Revenge of the Sith novel">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>}}
The '''IG-100 MagnaGuard''', also known as the '''MagnaGuard''', the '''IG-100 MagnaDroid''', the '''MagnaDroid''', or the '''Self-Motivating Heuristically Programmed Combat Droid''', was an advanced type of [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] that was used during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] as [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]], as per [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku's]] order, as well as being specialized infantry on the battlefield. After the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] secured Grievous's services as an enforcer, they refused to hire his [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]], and thus the [[Cyborg/Legends|cyborg]] general demanded a cadre of "more intelligent [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]]" to serve him. The construction of the MagnaGuards was then commissioned for Grievous's service, though the Jedi-killing droids were also occasionally employed to escort Count Dooku himself.

==Appearance and characteristics==
{{Quote|I saw an Intel report on this. I think they are Grievous's personal bodyguard droids. Prototypes built to his specifications. To fight Jedi.|Anakin Skywalker, to Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Revenge of the Sith novel" />}}
[[File:MagnaGuards-ROTSVG.jpg|thumb|left|220px|A pair of MagnaGuards]]
Constructed by [[Holowan Mechanicals/Legends|Holowan Mechanicals]], the IG-100 MagnaGuard, also known as the MagnaGuard,<ref name="ROTSTVD" /> the IG-100 MagnaDroid, the MagnaDroid,<ref name="Unknown Soldier">{{InsiderCite|86|Unknown Soldier: The Story of General Grievous}}</ref> or the Self-Motivating Heuristically Programmed Combat Droid were roughly two [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall, with a [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] body shape, but possessed a far-superior mechanical anatomy. This allowed for superhuman acrobatics, speed, and combat ability. Their internal systems were furnished with advanced combat learning programs, which, compared to most of the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] utilized by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], allowed the MagnaGuards to adapt to a highly diverse variety of tasks. These tasks ranged from melee and ranged combat to [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] control. The faces of the MagnaGuards featured two [[Color|red]]<ref name="ROTSTVD" /> or yellow [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptor]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], which were complemented by a backup system mounted on the chest.<ref name="Shadow Warrior" /> The droid's choice of [[Weapon/Legends|weapon]] was the [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]-resistant [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaff]], and they wore [[Clothing/Legends|head wraps]] and [[Cloak/Legends|cloaks]] that resembled that of [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]]'s old elite group of [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] and [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]], ''[[Izvoshra/Legends|Izvoshra]]'', when the [[General/Legends|general]] was a [[Kaleesh/Legends|Kaleesh]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]].<ref name="ROTSTVD" /> They were known to sport [[Mumuu/Legends|Mumuu]] markings on their [[Kaleesh cloak/Legends|cloaks]] matching those on [[Grievous's masks/Legends|Grievous' mask]].<ref name="CharEnc" /> Several models of the IG-100 existed, superficially denoted by color—black, alabaster, blue, and the rare gray were all spotted throughout the war. Each model had a specific programming, training, and thus specialty.<ref name="DB|droid|bodyguarddroid|Bodyguard droid">[[Databank (original)]]</ref> These droids were part of the same Holowan Mechanicals series as the later [[IG-88 assassin droid/Legends|IG-88]] line.<ref name="ROTSTVD" /> MagnaGuards were also capable of speech and were programmed to taunt their opponents in a low growling [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]].<ref name="Revenge of the Sith video game">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]]</ref> Aside from [[Human/Legends|Human]] speech, they appeared to occasionally use an audible form of [[Binary/Legends|droid language]].<ref name="Cargo of Doom">{{TCW|Cargo of Doom}}</ref> When in distress, such as when pinned to the ground, they also make yelping sounds.<ref name="Episode III">{{Film|III}}</ref>

===Hardiness===
MagnaGuards were fully optimized to battle and kill [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. This was due to not only their impeccable melee functionality but also their capability to withstand a massive loss of structural integrity before total system failure. Even after decapitation<ref name="Episode III" /> or bisection,<ref name="Revenge of the Sith video game" /> they could continue to effectively engage a target. The only sure way to destroy a MagnaGuard was to stab it in the chest.<ref name="Episode III" /> In addition, they were partially plated with strong [[Duranium/Legends|duranium]] [[Armor/Legends|armor]], making it very hard for even a Jedi to destroy them.<ref name="ROTSTVD" />

===Training===
{{Quote|The age of the Jedi is over.|An unknown MagnaGuard|<ref name="Revenge of the Sith video game" />}}
[[File:MagnaGuard-TCW.png|thumb|right|180px|A MagnaGuard ready for action.]]
General Grievous was given the bodyguards even though he was very impatient with droids due to their many limitations, such as limited artificial intelligence. [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] then commissioned Holowan Mechanicals to develop a cutting-edge warrior droid that would meet Grievous's standards. Upon activation, Grievous destroyed all the MagnaGuards present, venting his frustration at being treated as a droid.<ref name="The Eyes of Revolution">{{StoryCite|story=The Eyes of Revolution|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref> Grievous then personally trained the rest of his bodyguards in the seven classic styles of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] so they could effectively engage and kill Jedi. Grievous would not allow any minor repairs to be made to the droids, believing that their numerous scrapes and battle scars made them more intimidating to enemies.<ref name="ROTSTVD" /> Grievous engaged his bodyguards in practice fights as part of training, often damaging them in the process.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith novel" />

==Background==
===Clone Wars===
{{Quote|What in the galaxy was that?|[[Scorch/Legends|Scorch]], upon first sighting an IG-100|<ref name="Republic Commando">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref>}}
The droids were first used in combat during the [[Battle of Parein II 4/Legends|Battle of Parein II 4]], where one of Grievous's MagnaGuards killed the Jedi [[Sannen/Legends|Sannen]] by thrusting its electrostaff through his throat.<ref name="Unknown Soldier" /> The MagnaGuards soon proved to be formidable, capable of taking on Jedi and [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] with ease, and were regarded as being even more daunting than [[Droideka/Legends|droidekas]] by some.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith novel" /> Despite their many strengths, they were by no means invulnerable as [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] managed to momentarily incapacitate one with an ion stunner during the [[Battle of Xagobah (Clone Wars)|Second Battle of]] [[Xagobah/Legends|Xagobah]], though the bounty hunter was ultimately defeated and left for dead by Grievous himself.<ref name="Boba Fett: A New Threat">''[[Boba Fett: A New Threat]]''</ref> Along with their combat duties, General Grievous eventually began using MagnaGuards to do his dirty work, such as when they were used to torture Jedi Master [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Koth]] on [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]].<ref name="Grievous Intrigue">{{TCW|Grievous Intrigue}}</ref>

[[File:Dooku_MagnaGuards_TCW.png|thumb|left|250px|Three MagnaGuards accompany Dooku to [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]].]]
The MagnaGuards also played a role during [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano's]] mission to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. The Jedi were attacked in the exosphere by several MagnaGuards piloting [[Rogue-class Porax-38 starfighter/Legends|''Rogue''-class starfighters]]. After destroying the droids and reaching the surface of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]], Ahsoka Tano fought and destroyed three more MagnaGuards, while Anakin fought off Count Dooku.<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (film)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' film]]</ref>

During a mission to destroy a CIS [[Skytop Station/Legends|listening post]] near [[Ruusan/Legends|Ruusan]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] battled several MagnaGuards that were preventing [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] from being rescued.<ref name="Duel of the Droids">{{TCW|Duel of the Droids}}</ref>

MagnaGuards were present at [[Grievous's castle/Legends|Grievous's castle]] on [[Vassek/Legends|Vassek's]] [[Third moon of Vassek/Legends|third]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]]. Upon Grievous's return to his castle, he discovered his force of elite MagnaGuards had mysteriously been deactivated. When Count Dooku alerted him of the infiltration of his castle by Jedi Master [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]] and his former apprentice, [[Nahdar Vebb/Legends|Nahdar Vebb]], Grievous realized [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] himself had deactivated his guards to see if Grievous was adept in handling the Jedi by himself, as Grievous had recently suffered a chain of defeats. During this mission, one MagnaGuard was sent to destroy the [[Nu-class attack shuttle/Legends|Nu-class attack shuttle]] with a [[Missile launcher/Legends|rocket launcher]], while another squad was sent to destroy Kit Fisto's Jedi starfighter. However, Fisto's [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] managed to personally pilot the ship to safety. Meanwhile, Nahdar Vebb, who was already in the Castle, managed to destroy Grievous's entire escort of droids, only to be killed by Grievous himself.<ref name="Lair of Grievous" />

[[File:MagnaGuard_trio.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Three MagnaGuards protect Grievous's castle on the third moon of Vassek.]]
The bounty hunter, [[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]], while under contract with the CIS, was given several MagnaGuards for use in capturing the keeper of the [[Kyber memory crystal/Legends|kyber memory crystal]], Jedi Master [[Bolla Ropal/Legends|Bolla Ropal]]. One stood sentry as Cad Bane tortured the Jedi to [[Death/Legends|death]], afterward using its staff to crudely check for any vital response from the dead [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]].<ref name="Cargo of Doom" />

The droids were often employed to capture or kill Jedi, such as during the capture of Jedi Master [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]] over [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]]. The droids aided the General in getting the upper hand on Koth, surrounding the Jedi and slowly wearing him down with electrostaff strikes. Once Koth was captured, the droids tortured the Jedi in a transmission sent to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant. However, they were unaware that the Zabrak was still cognizant, resisting their torture, and sending a coded hand signal to alert the Jedi to his location.<ref name="Grievous Intrigue" /> Dooku also used MagnaGuards in subduing Anakin Skywalker during a [[Skirmish on Naboo/Legends|skirmish]] on Naboo. Dooku and the MagnaGuards were able to capture Skywalker in order conduct a prisoner exchange for General Grievous.<ref name="Shadow Warrior" />
Two of these droids were also used during the [[Battle of Boz Pity (Clone Wars)|Battle of Boz Pity]], under Dooku. During the battle, they distracted [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] long enough for the Count to make his escape, and one of them almost killed [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]] with a [[DC-15A blaster rifle/Legends|blaster]] under Dooku's orders.<ref name="Obsession">''[[Star Wars: Obsession]]''</ref>

[[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]] was forced to fight several MagnaGuards on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] during their [[Mission to Kashyyyk (Clone Wars)|rescue]] of the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] chieftain [[Tarfful/Legends|Tarfful]]. The [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]] managed to destroy the droids with great difficulty.<ref name="Republic Commando" />

[[File:MagnaGuard-Utapau.png|thumb|left|250px|A MagnaGuard on [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]].]]
Near the end of the war, MagnaGuards assisted Grievous in the kidnapping of [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]]. [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]] faced off dozens of MagnaGuards with difficulty before they retreated, alerting her to the Chancellor's danger.<ref name="CW23">{{CW|23}}</ref> This led to a rescue mission, in which Anakin Skywalker and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] fought two of the droids on the bridge of General Grievous's command ship, the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']], before rescuing the Chancellor.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith novel" /> Kenobi beheaded his opponent, only to find himself engaging a still-functioning headless droid. Skywalker managed to bisect the second droid as Kenobi finished the first off.<ref name="Episode III" />

Kenobi also faced four MagnaGuards on [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]] shortly before his fight with Grievous. He incapacitated three of them immediately upon using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to drop a large block of metal upon them. The fourth was partly pinned under the block, and then decapitated by Kenobi.<ref name="Episode III" />

===Post-Clone Wars===
Following the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|massacre]] of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] by Darth Vader, under [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious's]] orders, all IG-100 MagnaGuards were deactivated. However, the [[Geonosian/Legends|Geonosian]] [[Gizor Dellso]] would later reactivate and use IG-100 MagnaGuards as infantry in his personal army.<ref name="Battlefront II" /> At least a decade later, two MagnaGuards were reactivated by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] for use as [[N-K Necrosis]]'s bodyguards, and re-designated as [[NK-3]]s.<ref name="SWG:RotW">''[[Star Wars Galaxies: Rage of the Wookiees]]''</ref> In addition, a delivery was made for a [[TK-555]] bobble-head, a battlefield diorama, and blueprints for the IG-100 MagnaGuards.<ref name="SWG:TCOA">{{GalaxiesNGE}}</ref> The bureaucrat [[Narp Pilyev]] owned two MagnaGuards and used them as security guards, to protect his apartment on Coruscant.<ref name="SAV">[[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']]</ref>

==MagnaGuards in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Crush them! Make them suffer!|Grievous, to his MagnaGuards aboard the [[Invisible Hand/Legends|''Invisible Hand'']]|audio=MakeThemSuffer-ROTS.flac|<ref name="Episode III" />}}
===Notable units===
Distinguished MagnaGuards include [[IG-101/Legends|IG-101]] and [[IG-102/Legends|IG-102]], both of whom served on the ''Invisible Hand''.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith novel" /> Other MagnaGuards who were named were [[IG-109]] and [[IG-138]], who were both destroyed in a training session with Grievous. Another pair, [[IG-153]] and [[IG-182]] were employed by [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[4-8C]]. One of the most noteworthy MagnaGuards was [[IG-179]], [[Iron Knight]] [[Luxum (Jedi)|Luxum's]] chief [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]].<ref name="Lord of War">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/86/indexp2.html|text=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War|int=The Story of General Grievous: Lord of War}}</ref>

==Weapons and equipment==
===Armaments===
[[File:MagnaGuard-CN.png|thumb|left|180px|A MagnaGuard with electrostaff powered down]]
Grievous's bodyguards notably wielded high-quality [[Phrik/Legends|phrik]] alloy electrostaffs, blunt energy weapons which emitted a visible, pink, electromagnetic pulse on each end. The lightsaber-resistant nature of phrik allowed the MagnaGuards to effectively deflect and attack a Jedi's lightsaber. This, coupled with the specialized combat mechanics of the droids, made them a dangerous enemy, even to those skilled in the Force. Despite their specialization in electrostaffs, the on-board combat systems of the MagnaGuard, coupled with humanlike hands allowed them to be trained to operate a vast array of available weapons in addition to much more specialized armaments. Depending on the time and necessity, MagnaGuards were known to use blaster rifles,<ref name="Obsession" /> [[Bulldog RLR|grenades]], [[RPS-6 rocket launcher/Legends|rocket launchers]],<ref name="Lair of Grievous" /> remote-controlled [[Mark IV recon droid|drones]], and [[RD-4 grenade launcher|lethally irradiating weapons]] as well as regular melee weapons.

===On-board utilities===
Along with their weapons, the droids made use of many gadgets, such as built-in tow-cables, a personal [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]],<ref name="Republic Commando" /> and magnetized limbs.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith video game" /> At least one MagnaGuard was known to have the ability to extend its arm many times its usual length.<ref name="CW23" /> Another tool was a violent self destruct sequence, used if the system was still functional after severe damage. This was utilized by MagnaGuards who were encountered by clone commando squad [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta]] on Kashyyyk.<ref name="Republic Commando" /> In addition, these particular droids could fire pairs of small seeking missiles from internal magazines in their back plating.<ref name="DB|droid|bodyguarddroid|Bodyguard droid" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|General Kenobi, Anakin Skywalker. We've been waiting for you.|MagnaGuard from a deleted scene in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode III Revenge of the Sith: Illustrated Screenplay">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay'']]</ref>}}
Grievous's MagnaGuards were acted in ''Revenge of the Sith'' by stunt performers wearing green and blue jumpsuits, which were then replaced by computer-generated models.<ref name="DB|droid|bodyguarddroid|Bodyguard droid" /> The MagnaGuard design was originally proposed by concept artist [[Warren Fu]] as a design for Grievous himself. [[George Lucas]] then reviewed it and asked for Grievous's final appearance to be developed from it, but it was nonetheless eventually used as the MagnaGuard.<ref name="ROTS DVD bonuses">{{Film|III}} DVD bonuses</ref> In the original script of Episode III, MagnaGuards could talk, but this concept did not make it to the released film.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay'']]</ref>

In ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]'', as part of the Second Delivery subquest, the player has to obtain blueprints for the IG-100 MagnaGuards as one of the required items for the side quest. It along with two other required items (a TK-555 bobble-head and a battlefield diorama) were obtainable only through Email Collection system.<ref name="SWG:TCOA" />
